name: dnSpy - .NET Decompiler and Debugger
description: dnSpy is a Windows .NET assembly editor, decompiler, and debugger. It decompiles managed EXE/DLLs to readable C#/VB, lets you set breakpoints and step through IL at runtime, and edit+save assemblies (patch license/auth checks, bypass protections). Essential for reversing .NET malware, thick clients, and CTF binaries.
notes:
=== OPEN ===
  dnSpy.exe <file>                 # or drag the .exe/.dll into the GUI
  # (use dnSpyEx, the maintained fork; 32- and 64-bit builds)

=== READ ===
  - Assembly Explorer: namespaces -> types -> methods (decompiled to C#)
  - Right-click > Analyze: callers/callees, string usage
  - Edit > Search (Ctrl-Shift-K): "password", "connectionString", "key", "http"

=== DEBUG ===
  Debug > Start (F5) or Attach to Process; set breakpoints; inspect locals/IL

=== PATCH ===
  - Right-click a method > Edit Method (C#) or Edit IL Instructions
  - change a bool check / return value ; File > Save Module
  # e.g. force IsLicensed()/CheckAuth() to return true

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  ILSpy / dotPeek     # decompile (read-only)
  de4dot              # deobfuscate protected .NET
  Ghidra              # native + some managed
  x64dbg              # native debugging

recommended.note: .NET deserialization gadgets often found while reversing.

defense.why_it_works: .NET assemblies ship as IL with rich metadata, so decompilers reconstruct near-source C#. Without obfuscation, logic, secrets, and security checks are fully readable and editable, and the IL can be patched and re-saved.
defense.prerequisites: A copy of the managed assembly (EXE/DLL).
defense.impact: Recovery of connection strings/keys/logic, and the ability to patch out license/auth/integrity checks in the client.
defense.detection: Not detectable (offline analysis of a distributed assembly); tampered assemblies can be caught by strong-name/signature verification at load time.
defense.artifacts: None in the backend; strong-name or Authenticode verification failures if integrity checks exist.
defense.prevention: Obfuscate (ConfuserEx/commercial) and anti-tamper managed code; strong-name sign and verify assemblies; keep secrets server-side, not in the client; enforce auth/license on the server; native AOT for sensitive logic.
